messages:
devon: heads up — seeing a big uptick in pod connection resets from the westus2 gpu pool. started ~09:47 UTC, ~2000 pods showing transient grpc UNAVAILABLE and 502s.

marta: yikes. any errors in kube-proxy / conntrack logs?

devon: quick grep showed conntrack entries jumping then failing to accept new flows. sample from one node: 
```
# conntrack -L | tail -n 3
ipv4     2 tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.2.45.12 dst=10.8.1.23 sport=58022 dport=443 packets=218 bytes=36789 src=10.8.1.23 dst=10.2.45.12 sport=443 dport=58022 packets=200 bytes=34500
```
and `conntrack -S` shows entries ~= 262144 which matches nf_conntrack_max on the node.

alex: interesting. are these pods making lots of short-lived outbound connections? any prefetch pattern?

devon: yes — model prefetch for cold starts (gpupool-autoscaler) opened many concurrent exporter/registry requests across nodes. also some intra-cluster redis fanout spikes.

jin: is SNAT in play? I/O shows node SNAT used for pod->pod when cross-node. that can blow the ephemeral port table quickly.

marta: run `ss -s` on an impacted node? also `sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` value?

devon: ran both: `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 262144`; `ss -s` shows TCP: total 200k, established ~40k, time_wait ~150k. ephemeral port range is default 32768-60999.

ops-bot: alert created: CONNTRACK_HIGH westus2-gpupool (severity: high) — paging oncall.

alex: causes: (1) model prefetch concurrency + pod churn => many short lived outbound SNAT flows; (2) cross-node traffic due to autoscaler placement; (3) ip_local_port_range is tight so port reuse stalls, lots of TIME_WAIT.

jin: quick mitigation options: 
- lower prefetch concurrency in the autoscaler (reduce new outbound connections)
- increase nf_conntrack_max and buckets (short-term)
- widen ip_local_port_range to allow more ephemeral ports
- enable node-local model cache / move registry calls off-node-local (longer term)
- avoid SNAT by enabling Calico IP-per-pod or using Eni CNI where possible

marta: do we have capacity to bump conntrack on all westus2 nodes? risk: memory increase, but should be safe for short window.

devon: we can try a staggered sysctl patch via daemonset that increases net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max to 786432 and nf_conntrack_buckets accordingly. will monitor vm.memory, but it's doable.

alex: also put a temporary guard in autoscaler: throttle prefetch concurrency from 64 -> 8 per node for next 1 hour. that will dramatically cut new outbound flows.

marta: agree. plan: (A) patch autoscaler config to throttle prefetch now (owner: alex) (B) rollout conntrack sysctl daemonset to westus2 (owner: devon) (C) open config PR to widen ip_local_port_range on new node image (owner: jin) (D) add a node-level LRU model cache to reduce inter-node registry calls (owner: infra-research).

devon: doing (A) now. will push to prod config channel.

alex: i pushed canary with prefetch=8 to the gpupool-autoscaler group. monitoring traces.

sre-bot: grafana alert: Conntrack usage in westus2 -> decreased from 98% to 53% in 5m after canary.

devon: good signal. starting a conntrack bump daemonset rollout to 30% of nodes as safety. command snippet: 
```
kubectl apply -f conntrack-bump-daemonset.yaml
# sysctl set via privileged init: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=786432
```

marta: also add a temporary iptables rule to earlier drop SYN floods? cautious about side effects. maybe not necessary now.

jin: longer term notes: replace SNAT-heavy path by assigning pod IPs on ENI-backed nodes for gpupool, or using ipvs with direct pod routing. RDMA nodes: verify that RDMA traffic is not being SNATed — that would break performance.

devon: noted — RDMA-enabled racks are currently on-node-only traffic but autoscaler placed pods across RDMA+non-RDMA zones which caused fallback to TCP and extra connections. i'll add placement constraint to prefer RDMA pods on RDMA-capable nodes to reduce cross-node traffic.

alex: cost/ops tradeoff: increasing conntrack_max uses extra memory but avoids expensive pod churn and failed requests (which cause retries and higher cloud egress). short-term cost of memory < repeated GPU job failures.

marta: recording action items in infra runbook and will create a ticket to track root cause + followup (calico migration / node-local cache / autoscaler tuning).

devon: tl;dr: prefetch concurrency caused a rippleback of SNAT/conntrack exhaustion -> high grpc 5xx. mitigations applied: throttled prefetch (canary), conntrack bump daemonset (staggered), placement tweak for RDMA. monitoring looks healthy.

alex: thanks all — keep observing for next 2 hours, if any rollback needed ping @marta and @devon. :thumbsup:
